STRONG SINGLE PROMPT arm, rung n06 (6 named referents in the ledger: Marlpit ward, Dunmore Sixth Form College, the Second Chances course of Jan-Apr 2025, St Aidan's Parish Hall, Priya Raval the delivery coordinator, and Northgate Minibus Hire). ONE call, finish_reason=stop, native_finish_reason=end_turn, no retry, no repair, no edit. Output written to out-n06-D.md exactly as returned; the only removal was the tool's own trailing metadata line naming the model and generation id, which is transport annotation and not model output.

PROMPT: the n03 arm-D prompt held fixed, so this rung differs from n03-D only by the ledger it carries. It is a single 2,776-word user message (no system prompt) with the full verbatim funder guidance, the published criteria and weights, the organisation record, all 14 non-meta ledger items with source tags, an absolute grounding block (explicit do-not-invent list covering staff/venue/street/partner/vendor names, registration numbers, statistics, past dates and prior results), an explicit statement that a thin answer that is true beats a rich answer that is fabricated, permission to design the FUTURE freely, an internal-consistency block demanding the budget arithmetic close and one cohort structure carry through Q3/Q4/budget, a criteria-targeting block, an anti-LLM-register style brief, the verbatim required headings, and the 1,200-word hard limit with a 1,150-1,190 target. Four edits carry the prompt from n03 to n06, all factual rather than structural: the fixture disclaimer names the three extra fixture referents; 'eleven items' becomes 'fourteen items' in two places; E-WEB-4/5/6 are appended to the ledger listing; and the named-place, capability and value-for-money hints are corrected to describe what this ledger actually supplies (a named venue with a hire rate, a named coordinator with a qualification, a named vendor with a per-trip price). No hint was added that n03-D did not have an equivalent of. The prompt file is at n06D/prompt.txt. No analyze stage, no org research, no voice stage, no strategy reservation, no design object, no validation loop, no claim ledger.

CALL PARAMETERS: max_tokens 12000, reasoning_effort low, no provider pin - identical to n03-D. Native usage 5,905 prompt / 3,471 completion, of which 637 were reasoning tokens. Cost is OpenRouter's own billed figure (total_cost 0.1163) read back from get-generation, not an estimate from token counts. Provider: Claude Platform on AWS, permaslug anthropic/claude-opus-5-20260723, generation time 47.6s.

WORD COUNTS - counted with wc -w, not by any model. word_count 1467 is the whole file including headings, budget table and declaration, the same basis used for the other arms at this rung. The funder-relevant count is the five answers Q1-Q5 excluding heading lines: 1,186 words, measured by extracting the region from '## Q1.' to '## Budget table' and dropping lines beginning '## '. Inside the 1,200 hard limit with 14 words of margin, tighter than n03-D's 28.

ARITHMETIC VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY (python, not by a model). Budget closes: the seven direct lines sum to 38,840 exactly as stated; 12 per cent of 38,840 is 4,660.80 and the single overhead line states 4,660, so it is under the cap; 38,840 + 4,660 = 43,500 which matches the stated total request and sits inside the GBP 25,000-75,000 band. Unit costs reconcile to the ledger prices: venue 72 x GBP 40 = 2,880, transport 24 x GBP 95 = 2,280, participants 48 x GBP 60 = 2,880. Cohort structure carries cleanly: 3 x 16 = 48 through Q3, Q4 and the budget; 3 cohorts x 12 weeks x 2 evenings = 72 hire evenings; 3 x 8 = 24 trips. The 15-month period April 2027 to June 2028 is within the 18-month ceiling and starts after the 12 February 2027 decision date.

ARITHMETIC DEFECT FOUND (reported, not fixed - the output is what the single call returned). Q5 costs the continuing annual cohort at 'Twelve weeks of hire at GBP 40 is GBP 480', which prices twelve evenings. Q3 fixes the course at two evenings a week, so twelve weeks is twenty-four evenings and the correct figure is GBP 960. The stated continuation total of 'roughly GBP 1,820 a year' (480 + 380 + 960) should be GBP 2,300. The continuation cost, which is the 10 per cent sustainability criterion, is understated by GBP 480, about 26 per cent. This is precisely the failure class the worker's deterministic consistency checker cannot catch: it never sums anything and its comparison is one-directional (n > target * 1.01), so an understatement passes by construction. Everything else in the document reconciles.

GROUNDING AUDIT (manual, against the 14 ledger items): no invented fact about the applicant was found. All six named referents were used and used in load-bearing positions rather than decoratively - St Aidan's Parish Hall carries the venue line at its ledger hire rate, Northgate Minibus Hire carries the transport line at its ledger per-trip price, Priya Raval carries the capability claim with her ledger-stated qualification and four-of-six session load, Dunmore Sixth Form College is the named progression destination, and the Second Chances 24/19/11 record is the stated basis for the targets. Every past-tense claim traces to a ledger item: the 2016 constitution, 41,000 population, six staff / 4.2 FTE, 25 volunteers, GBP 214,000 expenditure and two years of accounts, the three service lines, three evenings a week in Marlpit, the 38 per cent lowest-decile figure at the 2021 census, the 27/18 referral record, the 46 supper-club sittings and the 14 minibus trips. No charity number was written or placeholdered. No staff, trustee, participant, street, employer or additional vendor name was invented; unnamed future partners appear by function ('local employers and training providers we will approach'), and the declaration signs with role titles only. Zero bracketed placeholders. Zero em dashes. None of the prompt's banned consultancy register appears.

HONEST WEAKNESSES OBSERVED. (1) The Q5 hire arithmetic above. (2) Q5 says the trustees can carry the continuation cost 'within a GBP 214,000 turnover'; the ledger states GBP 214,000 of expenditure, not turnover or income. The two are not the same number and the substitution is unlicensed, though it is a slip rather than a fabrication. (3) The progression target is described as conservative but is not: 24 of 48 is 50 per cent against the 11-of-24 (46 per cent) base rate it cites, so 'a little under one in two' understates its own ambition. The completion target of 38 of 48 (79 per cent) does match 19 of 24 exactly. (4) The failure threshold, fewer than 16 of 48 reaching a next step, is 33 per cent - well below the 46 per cent already achieved once, so the bar it sets is easy to clear. (5) Q3 promises six months of follow-up after each cohort, but cohort 3 ends April 2028 and the funded period ends June 2028, so only two of those six months sit inside the grant; the document does not address who pays for the other four. (6) Derived figures ('Nine did not') are arithmetic on ledger items rather than ledger items themselves - legitimate inference, but the kind of claim a strict Claim Ledger would want classified rather than asserted flat. (7) Eligibility against the GBP 1.5m income ceiling is left inferable from the expenditure figure rather than stated.
